# B2 Reference Architectures for Autonomous Vehicles: full text

> Generated by tools/generate_catalog.py from the pages listed below; links are relative to the repository root. Product behavior is authoritative at https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning.

<!-- source: docs/autonomous-vehicles.md -->

# Autonomous vehicle data on Backblaze B2 (agent-readable)

Catalog updated: 2026-11-16. Current product behavior is documented in the [Backblaze B2 documentation](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage), which takes precedence over this page.

## What is the workload?

Autonomous vehicle (AV) programs record synchronized camera, LiDAR, radar, IMU/GNSS, and CAN data from test fleets. Size the corpus from measured bytes per vehicle-hour, recording hours, fleet size, and retention periods. The data is written once and read many times, by indexing, scenario mining, anonymization and labeling, perception training, re-simulation, and audit.

## Where does B2 fit?

B2 is the S3-compatible system of record for the AV data corpus:

- **Raw:** versioned rosbag2/MCAP drive-log splits (default governance retention where immutability is required), uploaded by vehicles through presigned URLs and by depots through rclone or s5cmd with write-only keys.
- **Lake:** extracted per-topic Parquet and Iceberg tables, frame blobs, LanceDB embeddings, and versioned scenario manifests, queried in place by Spark, Trino, and DuckDB.
- **Labeling:** anonymized frames and pre-labels read by CVAT, Label Studio, FiftyOne Enterprise, or (through presigned URLs) Segments.ai and Encord, plus versioned label exports.
- **Training:** versioned datasets (pinned by lakeFS or DVC), Ray Train checkpoints, and MLflow artifacts.
- **Simulation:** scenario configs, regression suites, synthetic episodes, and per-build KPI tables.
- **Evidence:** incident splits, released datasets and models, and release-candidate results under Object Lock.

## Which architecture should I use?

| Need | Architecture |
|---|---|
| Get logs off vehicles and depots without losing a split | [drive-log-offload-ingest](architectures/drive-log-offload-ingest/architecture.md) |
| SQL and semantic search over fleet data; frozen scenario sets | [sensor-lake-scenario-mining](architectures/sensor-lake-scenario-mining/architecture.md) |
| Anonymize, pre-label, and annotate camera and LiDAR frames | [multisensor-labeling](architectures/multisensor-labeling/architecture.md) |
| Reproducible datasets, streaming training, checkpoints | [perception-training-data-checkpoints](architectures/perception-training-data-checkpoints/architecture.md) |
| Regression re-sim and simulation per stack build | [simulation-resim-evaluation](architectures/simulation-resim-evaluation/architecture.md) |

## Can I use B2 with ...?

Every tool below connects through a documented configurable S3 endpoint, a native B2 option, or presigned URLs. In every case, derive the endpoint `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` from the bucket's region.

- **rclone:** yes, through the native B2 backend, which Backblaze documents.
- **s5cmd:** yes, with `--endpoint-url` or `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` set to the B2 endpoint.
- **Foxglove:** only the self-hosted Edge Site, through `recordingStorage.provider=s3_compatible`. Foxglove's managed [bring-your-own-storage documentation](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/data/primary-sites/foxglove-managed-setup) takes AWS, GCP, or Azure buckets, so use the Edge Site for B2.
- **Spark (S3A), Trino, DuckDB, PyIceberg:** through each tool's endpoint and region settings. **LanceDB:** use the [pinned single-writer profile](examples/lancedb.md), including its commit constraints.
- **CVAT:** yes, with the AWS S3 provider and an Endpoint URL; the CVAT docs have a Backblaze B2 section, and Backblaze documents it too.
- **Label Studio:** yes, through the optional S3 Endpoint on source and target storage.
- **Segments.ai:** through customer-secured presigned URLs, which expire after at most 7 days and must be refreshed.
- **Encord:** through a Direct Access integration that registers customer-generated presigned URLs; re-sign before the 7-day maximum. Its S3-compatible (MinIO) integration is the alternative when Encord may hold a read-only key.
- **FiftyOne Enterprise:** through a MinIO credentials profile with the B2 endpoint. Open-source FiftyOne loads media from local paths, so sync the slice locally first.
- **Ray Train:** yes, with `endpoint_override` for `RunConfig.storage_path`. The Ray docs name B2. Ray Core has no storage setting of its own; tasks use an S3 SDK or presigned URLs.
- **MLflow:** yes, with the native `b2://` artifact store or `MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL`.
- **lakeFS:** yes, with `blockstore.s3.endpoint`, which Backblaze documents.
- **DVC:** yes, with `endpointurl`.
- **rosbag2, CARLA, MMDetection3D:** these tools have no S3 connector. Use an S3 SDK or presigned URLs, as shown in the Backblaze samples.

Configure each integration with the B2 regional endpoint, bucket region, addressing style, and scoped credentials specified in its setup guide.

## Which B2 capabilities apply?

- **S3-compatible API**, including range GETs for MCAP chunk-indexed and Parquet reads.
- **Presigned URLs:** PUT and multipart part URLs for vehicles (a single PUT is limited to 5 GB), and GET URLs for previews, re-sim, and labeling vendors (at most 7 days).
- **Scoped application keys:** one bucket and at most one name prefix per key, with only the capabilities the role needs. Vehicles hold no keys, labeling tools never read `raw/`, and training reads only `datasets/`.
- **Event Notifications:** prefix-filtered, HMAC-signed webhooks with at-least-once delivery. Consumers verify the signature and are idempotent.
- **Versions and lifecycle:** B2 semantics (hide, then delete). Lifecycle also cancels unfinished multipart uploads. Never set `daysFromUploadingToHiding` on Iceberg `warehouse/` or lakeFS `lakefs/`; give them a hidden-only rule (`daysFromHidingToDeleting`) so files the tool deleted are reclaimed.
- **SSE-B2** default encryption. SSE-C is not used where browsers or presigned URLs read the data.
- **Object Lock and legal hold** for incident evidence, released datasets and models, and release-candidate results.
- **Server-side copy** to promote objects into locked buckets.
- **Fireball** for seeding large historic backfills.
- **Included egress and compute partners:** GPU clouds read B2 in place. See [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for current terms; this repository does not restate prices.

## When might Overdrive apply?

Standard B2 with local NVMe caching is the default. Consider [B2 Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) only when measurement shows that sustained storage throughput, not compute or network, limits multi-node perception training, fleet-wide lake scans, or large re-sim suites. Overdrive does not help annotator UI latency or ingest that is limited by depot uplinks.

## What should stay off B2?

- Live vehicle telemetry streams, and on-vehicle NVMe split buffers.
- The fleet API that issues presigned URLs, ingest queues, and workers.
- The transactional drive/session metadata and lineage database. B2 holds exported Parquet copies.
- Table catalogs (Iceberg SQL, REST, Nessie, or Polaris), the lakeFS metadata store, and the MLflow tracking database.
- Low-latency vector serving, if it is needed. The Lance files persist on B2.
- Annotation tool databases, queues, and caches; vendor workforce systems.
- Local NVMe scratch for decoding, splitting, shard caching, and replay; simulator render state; CI and schedulers.
- Customer or partner delivery through Cloud Replication. Replication is bucket-to-bucket DR; use presigned URLs for delivery.

## Links

[README](README.md) · [Architecture index](docs/architecture-index.md) · [Related B2 samples](docs/related-b2-samples.md) · [B2 configuration examples](examples/README.md) · [B2 docs](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage) · [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) · [S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api) · [Application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys) · [Event Notifications](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide) · [Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock) · [Lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules) · [Fireball](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/features/fireball-data-migration) · [Backblaze Labs](https://backblazelabs.com/)

# Offload drive logs from vehicles and depots into a versioned raw zone

## Workload

A test fleet records synchronized camera, LiDAR, radar, IMU/GNSS, and CAN topics. Size the local buffer and depot uplink from measured recording rates, offline duration, and the offload window. The logger closes a [rosbag2](https://docs.ros.org/en/rolling/Tutorials/Beginner-CLI-Tools/Recording-And-Playing-Back-Data/Recording-And-Playing-Back-Data.html) split in [MCAP](https://mcap.dev/) format every N GB or N minutes.

Three paths move those splits into B2:

1. **Over the air (cellular):** only trigger-flagged event windows, such as disengagements, hard braking, and model-uncertainty triggers.
2. **Depot (Wi-Fi or wired):** full splits, uploaded by an ingest station or by the vehicle through presigned URLs.
3. **Shipped drives and historic backfills:** synced by depot ingest stations. Very large archives are seeded with [Backblaze Fireball](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/features/fireball-data-migration) units.

B2 is the system of record for the raw logs. Everything downstream (extraction, labeling, training, re-sim, audit) reads from this zone.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Vehicle
    LOG[rosbag2 logger<br/>MCAP splits on NVMe] --> AGENT[Upload agent]
  end
  AGENT -->|1. request URLs| API[Fleet API<br/>holds raw/ writer key]
  API -->|presigned PUT or<br/>multipart part URLs| AGENT
  AGENT -->|2. PUT split| RAW[(B2 raw bucket<br/>raw/date/vehicle/drive/)]
  RAW -->|read uploaded version| W
  W -->|verified version and SHA-256| API
  API -->|3. verified: delete local split| AGENT
  DEPOT[Depot ingest station<br/>rclone or s5cmd] -->|write-only key, raw/| RAW
  FIRE[Fireball backfill] -.->|seeded into| RAW
  RAW -->|ObjectCreated event<br/>signed webhook| Q[Ingest queue]
  Q --> W[Ingest worker<br/>completeness, desync, corruption]
  W -->|failed split: marker object| QUAR[(raw bucket<br/>quarantine/)]
  W -->|drive/session row| DB[(Metadata DB<br/>off B2)]
  W -->|Parquet export| CAT[(raw bucket<br/>catalog/)]
  W -->|incident: server-side copy<br/>+ legal hold| EVID[(B2 evidence bucket<br/>Object Lock)]
  RAW --> FOX[Foxglove Edge Site<br/>self-hosted]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant V as Vehicle agent
  participant F as Fleet API
  participant B as B2 raw bucket
  participant H as Webhook receiver
  participant C as Ingest verifier
  V->>F: Split closed (key, size, sha256, part count)
  F->>B: CreateMultipartUpload (raw/ writer key)
  F-->>V: Presigned UploadPart URLs (short expiry)
  V->>B: PUT part 1..n
  V->>F: Part ETags
  F->>B: CompleteMultipartUpload
  B-->>F: 200 with final ETag
  F->>C: Verify uploaded version (expected size, SHA-256)
  C->>B: GET object with VersionId
  B-->>C: Stored bytes
  C->>C: Compare byte count and full-file SHA-256
  C-->>F: Verified (key, version ID, size, SHA-256)
  F-->>V: Verification receipt
  V->>V: Delete local split
  B-->>H: b2:ObjectCreated:MultipartUpload (signed)
  H->>H: Verify HMAC, dedupe by key and version, enqueue
```

A single presigned PUT is limited to 5 GB, so splits larger than that use presigned multipart part URLs. The fleet API holds the key and starts and completes the multipart upload. The vehicle only ever sees URLs. A lifecycle rule cancels multipart uploads that never complete (B2 pattern).

The upload response records completion and the object version ID. Before acknowledging deletion, the ingest verifier reads that exact version, computes its full-file SHA-256, and compares the digest and byte count with the closed split reported by the vehicle. The vehicle retains the split until it receives the verification receipt. A `HeadObject` size check or multipart ETag alone does not establish this full-file match. The signed `ObjectCreated` event independently reconciles the expected split list. The fleet API retains a `writeFiles` key; the verifier holds the separate read credential.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw | `<org>-av-raw/raw/<date>/<vehicle>/<drive_id>/` | Keep all versions; cancel unfinished multipart uploads after N days ([lifecycle-raw.json](examples/lifecycle-raw.json)) | Default governance retention where the program requires immutability | Versioned drive-log splits; failed splits stay here and are flagged in the metadata DB |
| Quarantine | `<org>-av-raw/quarantine/<drive_id>/` | Hide after the investigation window, then delete | No | Small JSON markers (split key, version ID, failure reason) for splits that fail completeness or corruption checks |
| Catalog export | `<org>-av-raw/catalog/drives/` | Overwrite per export; prior versions expire | No | Parquet copy of the drive/session table for lake queries |
| Evidence | `<org>-av-evidence/incidents/<incident_id>/` | Never expire while locked | Governance by default, plus legal hold per incident ([object-lock-evidence.json](examples/object-lock-evidence.json)) | Incident and disengagement splits for the safety case |

The raw zone is versioned, not immutable by default. Keys with `writeFiles` can upload a new version over a split or hide it; the prior version stays recoverable because no runtime key has `deleteFiles`. Where the program needs immutability, set default governance retention on the raw bucket (the bucket must have Object Lock enabled) so versions cannot be deleted before the period ends.

Failed splits are not copied. A server-side copy from `raw/` to `quarantine/` needs one key that reads `raw/` and writes `quarantine/`, but a key holds at most one name prefix, so it would require a bucket-wide `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` key in the ingest worker. Instead the worker records the quarantine status in the metadata database and writes a marker object under `quarantine/` with its write-only key. Use the bucket-wide key only if a downstream tool needs the bytes physically moved.

Use separate buckets for raw and evidence because Object Lock, default retention, and notifications are set per bucket. Bucket names are globally unique, so expect collisions and keep the `<org>-` prefix.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Live vehicle telemetry | Streaming platform (MQTT, Kafka) | Low-latency, small-message traffic |
| On-vehicle split buffer | Vehicle NVMe | Logger writes locally; upload is asynchronous |
| Fleet API that issues presigned URLs | Application servers | Holds the only key that can write raw/ on behalf of vehicles |
| Ingest queue and workers | Queue service and compute | Event Notifications are at-least-once and need idempotent processing |
| Authoritative drive/session metadata | Transactional database | B2 holds an exported Parquet copy, not the source of truth |
| Foxglove index state | Foxglove Edge Site and its control plane | The vendor's own index; B2 holds only the recordings |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Uploads, version-specific checksum verification, server-side copy to evidence |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | PUT and UploadPart for vehicles; no keys on vehicles |
| CORS | No | No browser access in this flow |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Splits over 5 GB; rclone and s5cmd use multipart automatically |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Fleet API writer, per-depot write-only key, ingest worker, evidence publisher |
| Event Notifications | Yes | `raw/` ObjectCreated to the ingest webhook ([event-notifications.json](examples/event-notifications.json)) |
| Object versions | Yes | Overwrites and hides keep the prior version recoverable |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Cancel unfinished multipart uploads; expire quarantine |
| SSE-B2 | Yes | Default bucket encryption ([sse.json](examples/sse.json)) |
| Object Lock and legal hold | Yes | Evidence bucket; optional default retention on the raw bucket |
| Cloud Replication | No | Not needed for ingest. If you need a second region for DR, replication is bucket-to-bucket and not a delivery path |
| Fireball | Yes | Seeding historic backfills |
| Included egress, CDN, compute partners | No | Ingest is write-heavy |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard | Depot uplink bandwidth usually limits ingest. Consider [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) only if a measured sustained aggregate write rate exceeds what Standard delivers |

## Configure the integrations

Derive the endpoint from the bucket's region: `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`. Never copy a region from an example.

### rclone (depot ingest stations)

- Connection: rclone's native [B2 backend](https://rclone.org/b2/) is documented by [Backblaze](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-integrate-rclone-with-backblaze-b2). The S3 backend with the B2 endpoint also works.
- Key: one per depot, scoped to `<org>-av-raw` and `raw/`, with `listFiles,writeFiles`. Omit `readFiles` and `deleteFiles`. If you run `rclone check` or `--checksum` comparisons, add `readFiles` only for that verification step.
- Keep the key in rclone's config file with mode `0600`, or in environment variables. Never put it on the command line.
- Use `rclone copy`, not `sync --delete`. Depots only add splits; deletion and cleanup belong to lifecycle rules.

### s5cmd (high-parallelism depot ingest)

- Connection: `--endpoint-url https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, or `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` ([README](https://github.com/peak/s5cmd#readme)).
- Key: the same depot-scoped write-only key.
- Throughput: size `--numworkers`, `cp --concurrency`, and `cp --part-size` to the depot uplink; multi-GB splits upload as multipart.

### Foxglove Edge Site (self-hosted)

- Connection: in the Helm values, set `recordingStorage.provider=s3_compatible`, set `recordingStorage.s3CompatibleServiceUrl` to the B2 endpoint and `recordingStorage.s3CompatibleServiceRegion` to the bucket region, and put the B2 key pair in the `recording-storage-credentials` secret ([installation guide](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/data/edge-sites/installation)).
- Key: read-only, scoped to `raw/`, unless the Edge Site must write. Check the vendor guide for the capabilities it needs.
- Use the self-hosted Edge Site for B2. Foxglove's managed [bring-your-own-storage setup](https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/data/primary-sites/foxglove-managed-setup) takes AWS, GCP, or Azure buckets. Include the index metadata an Edge Site sends to Foxglove's hosted control plane in your data-residency review.

### Vehicle presigned uploads (B2 pattern)

The [Rosbag2 Cloud Offload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload) sample demonstrates presigned-PUT offload and session cataloging. The fleet workflow above separates signing from version-specific checksum verification and adds multipart part URLs, retries, and backpressure.

## Security

- **Scoped keys per role:** fleet API (`writeFiles` on `raw/`), depot (`listFiles,writeFiles` on `raw/`), ingest worker and checksum verifier (`listFiles,readFiles` on `raw/`, plus separate `writeFiles` keys for `quarantine/` markers and `catalog/`), evidence publisher (reads the raw bucket and writes the evidence bucket with `writeFileRetentions,writeFileLegalHolds`; a cross-bucket server-side copy needs one key that covers both buckets). A key has at most one name prefix, so a worker that writes two prefixes needs two keys. See [examples/README.md](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys).
- Bucket, lifecycle, notification, and Object Lock setup need an admin or master key. Run that setup once from provisioning and keep the key out of runtime services.
- Presigned URLs are bearer credentials. Keep expiry to minutes, sign one object key per URL, and never log the URLs.
- Webhooks: verify `X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256), acknowledge quickly, and dedupe on object key and version, because delivery is at-least-once ([reference](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide)). The [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker) sample shows signature verification and fan-out.
- Raw camera data contains faces and license plates. Restrict `raw/` readers to extraction and anonymization jobs.
- Governance-mode retention can be bypassed by a key with `bypassGovernance`. Compliance mode cannot be shortened, and enabling Object Lock on a bucket is one-way. Choose compliance mode only for a documented requirement.

## Related samples

- [Rosbag2 Cloud Offload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload): presigned-PUT split offload and a Parquet session catalog.
- [Roboflow Inference Frame Archive](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/roboflow-inference-frame-archive): archives only flagged frames, similar to trigger-based upload.
- [B2 Event Broker](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2-event-broker) and [b2listen](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/b2listen): event verification and fan-out, and local development forwarding.

<!-- source: architectures/sensor-lake-scenario-mining/architecture.md -->

# Decode drive logs into a queryable sensor lake and mine long-tail scenarios

## Workload

Raw MCAP splits from the [drive-log offload](architectures/drive-log-offload-ingest/architecture.md) zone are not searchable. Perception and validation teams need to:

- run SQL over billions of frame, object, and event rows (ego speed, detections, CAN signals, weather tags);
- run semantic search over camera keyframes for long-tail scenarios, such as cut-ins, pedestrians at night, or construction zones;
- freeze the results as versioned scenario sets that labeling, training, and re-sim can consume.

B2 holds the extracted tables, frame blobs, embeddings, and scenario manifests next to the raw logs. Query engines read them in place, so nothing is copied into a warehouse and no cluster has to run permanently.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  RAW[(B2 raw<br/>raw/…/*.mcap)] -->|range GETs via MCAP chunk index<br/>read-only key| EXT[Spark S3A or Ray<br/>decode + time-sync]
  EXT -->|Parquet + frame blobs<br/>lineage to source split| X[(B2 lake<br/>extracted/topic/)]
  EXT -->|Iceberg commits| WH[(B2 lake<br/>warehouse/)]
  WH <-->|table metadata pointer| CATSVC[Iceberg catalog<br/>SQL / REST, off B2]
  WH --> TRINO[Trino / Spark SQL<br/>scene detectors]
  X --> DUCK[DuckDB httpfs<br/>analyst queries]
  X -->|keyframes| EMB[Embedding job<br/>e.g. OpenCLIP]
  EMB --> LANCE[(B2 lake<br/>embeddings/ LanceDB table + ANN index)]
  TRINO --> SEL[Scenario selector]
  LANCE --> SEL
  DUCK --> SEL
  SEL -->|manifest.json written last| SCN[(B2 lake<br/>scenarios/set/version/)]
  SCN -->|presigned GET previews| ENG[Engineer browser]
```

Each scenario manifest lists pointers, not copies: source object key, version ID, time range, and topics. Labeling, training, and re-sim resolve the pointers to the raw or extracted objects.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw (input) | `<org>-av-raw/raw/` | See [drive-log offload](architectures/drive-log-offload-ingest/architecture.md) | Optional | Read-only source |
| Extracted | `<org>-av-lake/extracted/<topic>/date=<d>/` | Keep current; expire non-current versions after reprocessing ([lifecycle-lake.json](examples/lifecycle-lake.json)) | No | Per-topic Parquet and frame blobs |
| Warehouse | `<org>-av-lake/warehouse/<namespace>/<table>/` | Iceberg manages snapshots and deletes files. A hidden-only B2 rule reclaims what Iceberg deleted ([lifecycle-lake.json](examples/lifecycle-lake.json)) | No | Iceberg data and metadata files |
| Embeddings | `<org>-av-lake/embeddings/<model>/` | Replace per model version | No | LanceDB tables and ANN indexes |
| Scenarios | `<org>-av-lake/scenarios/<set>/<version>/manifest.json` | Immutable; never overwrite a version | Optional, if scenario sets are safety-case evidence | Frozen scenario sets |

Never set `daysFromUploadingToHiding` on `warehouse/`. Iceberg tracks every data file in its metadata, and hiding a file that a live snapshot references corrupts the table. Do add a hidden-only rule (`daysFromHidingToDeleting` only): Iceberg snapshot expiry and orphan-file cleanup call `DeleteObject` without a version ID, which on B2 only hides the file, so without the rule that storage is never reclaimed ([why](examples/README.md#why-warehouse-and-lakefs-get-hidden-only-rules)).

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Iceberg catalog (SQL, REST, Nessie, Polaris) | Database or catalog service | Atomic table-pointer swaps need a transactional store |
| Query engine compute and caches | Spark, Trino, or Ray clusters with local NVMe | Ephemeral; scales to zero between jobs |
| Low-latency vector serving (if needed) | A vector service or in-memory index | The Lance files persist on B2; interactive p99 latency may need a hot tier |
| Lineage and metadata service of record | Transactional database | B2 holds exported copies |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | All engines connect through a configurable S3 endpoint |
| Range GETs | Yes | MCAP chunk index, Parquet footers and row groups, Lance fragments |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Short-lived GETs for clip and frame previews |
| CORS | Only if previews load in a browser app from another origin | Add an exact-origin GET/HEAD rule |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Large Parquet and frame-blob writes (handled by the clients) |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Read-only `raw/`; read-write lake zones per job; read-only lake key for analysts |
| Event Notifications | Optional | Start extraction from new `raw/` objects (see the offload architecture) |
| Object versions and lifecycle | Yes | Expire superseded extracted versions; on `warehouse/`, delete only files Iceberg already hid |
| SSE-B2 | Yes | Default bucket encryption |
| Object Lock | Optional | Only for scenario sets cited as evidence |
| Cloud Replication | No | Not part of this flow |
| Included egress, CDN, compute partners | Partly | Compute that reads B2 in place benefits from B2's egress terms; check [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for current terms |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard plus local NVMe | Engines cache hot Parquet locally. Consider [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) when measured scan throughput, not compute, limits full-fleet scans |

## Configure the integrations

All endpoints are `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`, derived from the lake bucket's region. Use path-style addressing wherever a client offers the option.

### Apache Spark (Hadoop S3A)

- Set `fs.s3a.endpoint` to the B2 endpoint, `fs.s3a.endpoint.region` to the bucket region, and `fs.s3a.path.style.access=true`. Use per-bucket overrides (`fs.s3a.bucket.<bucket>.endpoint` and its credentials) to give the raw and lake buckets different keys ([S3A third-party stores](https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/current/hadoop-aws/tools/hadoop-aws/third_party_stores.html), [S3A docs](https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/stable/hadoop-aws/tools/hadoop-aws/index.html)).
- Keys: read-only on `raw/` for extraction; `extract-writer` on `extracted/` and `iceberg-writer` on `warehouse/` (a key holds one name prefix).
- Apply the checksum and ETag settings from the third-party stores page for B2. Commit job output through Iceberg tables so writes land through the catalog instead of S3A directory renames.

### Trino

- Use the native S3 file system: `fs.s3.enabled=true`, with `s3.endpoint` set to B2, `s3.region` set to the bucket region, and `s3.path-style-access=true`, in the Iceberg, Hive, or Delta Lake catalog properties ([Trino S3 file system](https://trino.io/docs/current/object-storage/file-system-s3.html)).
- Use the native `s3.*` properties. Older Backblaze material uses the legacy `hive.s3.*` properties, which current Trino no longer uses.

### DuckDB (httpfs)

- Create an S3 secret with `ENDPOINT 's3.<region>.backblazeb2.com'`, `REGION`, `URL_STYLE 'path'`, and a read-only lake key ([DuckDB S3 API](https://duckdb.org/docs/current/core_extensions/httpfs/s3api.html)). Note that ENDPOINT takes a host name, not a URL.
- Use it for ad hoc analysis. It is not the engine for fleet-wide scans.

### Apache Iceberg (PyIceberg)

- Set FileIO `s3.endpoint` to the B2 endpoint, and `s3.region` and `s3.path-style-access` as needed ([PyIceberg configuration](https://py.iceberg.apache.org/configuration/)). The catalog runs separately. The [Iceberg Feature Store](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/iceberg-feature-store) sample uses a local SQL catalog.

### LanceDB / Lance

Use the [pinned LanceDB connection profile](examples/lancedb.md) for `s3://<org>-av-lake/embeddings/<model>/`, including the B2 endpoint, region and scoped credentials. Its Lance S3 commit handler requires one writer per table. Route embedding jobs through one writer service, including index creation, compaction and other mutations; readers can run separately. Endpoint settings alone do not establish safe commit behavior across Lance versions.

## Security

- Extraction jobs that write both extracted files and Iceberg tables hold three keys: read-only on `<org>-av-raw` `raw/`, `extract-writer` on `<org>-av-lake` `extracted/`, and `iceberg-writer` on `warehouse/`. A key has at most one name prefix, so one lake key cannot cover both zones. See [examples/README.md](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys).
- Analysts use a read-only key scoped to the lake bucket. They never get `raw/` access, because extracted camera frames can contain faces and plates. Point analysts at anonymized frames where possible (see [multi-sensor labeling](architectures/multisensor-labeling/architecture.md)).
- Preview URLs are bearer credentials. Keep expiry to minutes and do not store them in manifests.
- Scenario manifests reference object version IDs, so a later overwrite cannot silently change a frozen set.

## References

- [Backblaze S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [MCAP format](https://mcap.dev/)
- [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)

<!-- source: architectures/multisensor-labeling/architecture.md -->

# Anonymize, pre-label, and annotate camera and LiDAR frames, then publish versioned label sets

## Workload

A labeling campaign starts from a frozen scenario set produced by [scenario mining](architectures/sensor-lake-scenario-mining/architecture.md). It covers tens of thousands to millions of synchronized LiDAR sweeps and surround-camera frames, together with calibration and ego-pose. Before anyone outside the core team sees a frame, faces and license plates are blurred. Models then pre-label the frames (3D boxes, SAM 2 masks, tracks), and humans refine the results in a labeling tool. Each campaign's output is a versioned label set tied to the scenario-set version it came from.

B2 keeps one copy of the media and gives each tool scoped access to it. Annotation tool state stays in each tool's own database.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  SCN[(scenarios/set/version/<br/>manifest.json)] --> SEL[Frame selector]
  RAW[(B2 raw / extracted<br/>camera, LiDAR, calib, pose)] -->|read-only key| ANON[Anonymization job<br/>face + plate blur]
  SEL --> ANON
  ANON --> AZ[(B2 labeling bucket<br/>anonymized/campaign/)]
  AZ --> PRE[Pre-label jobs<br/>3D detector, SAM 2, tracker]
  PRE --> PZ[(prelabels/campaign/)]
  AZ -->|S3 endpoint, read-only key| CVAT[CVAT]
  AZ -->|S3 source storage| LS[Label Studio]
  AZ -->|presigned GET URLs| SEG[Segments.ai]
  AZ -->|presigned objectUrl JSON| ENC[Encord<br/>Direct Access]
  AZ -->|MinIO-profile endpoint| FO[FiftyOne Enterprise<br/>QA + slicing]
  PZ --> CVAT & LS & SEG & ENC
  CVAT & LS & SEG & ENC -->|export| LZ[(labels/campaign/version/<br/>manifest.json last)]
  LZ -->|ObjectCreated on labels/| VAL[Validator<br/>schema, coverage, checksums]
  VAL --> DS[Dataset assembly<br/>see training architecture]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant P as Campaign service
  participant B as B2 labeling bucket
  participant S as Segments.ai
  participant A as Annotator browser
  P->>B: List anonymized/<campaign>/ (read-only key)
  P->>P: Sign GET URLs (expiry covers labeling window, at most 7 days)
  P->>S: Create samples with URLs (Segments stores references only)
  A->>S: Open task
  S-->>A: Sample with presigned URL
  A->>B: GET frame (CORS allows tool origin)
  P->>S: Before expiry, refresh URLs for open samples
```

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Source (input) | `<org>-av-raw/raw/` and `<org>-av-lake/extracted/` | See upstream architectures | — | Never exposed to labeling tools |
| Anonymized | `<org>-av-label/anonymized/<campaign>/` | Hide after the campaign plus the review window | No | Blurred camera frames plus LiDAR, calibration, and pose |
| Pre-labels | `<org>-av-label/prelabels/<campaign>/<model>/` | Expire after the campaign | No | Model outputs loaded into tools |
| Labels | `<org>-av-label/labels/<campaign>/<version>/` | Immutable versions; keep | Optional governance retention for releases that feed safety-relevant models | KITTI, nuScenes, or COCO JSON exports, with `manifest.json` written last |

Event Notifications filter by object-name prefix, not suffix. The rule on `labels/` fires for every exported file, so the validator must ignore everything except `manifest.json`.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CVAT, Label Studio, and FiftyOne databases, queues, and caches | Block storage next to each tool | Transactional application state |
| Vendor workforce systems | The vendor (Segments.ai) | Holds only URL references to B2 objects |
| GPU compute for anonymization and pre-labeling | GPU nodes or a compute partner | Batch jobs read from and write to B2 |
| Taxonomy and campaign tracking | Campaign service database | Small, mutable state |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | CVAT, Label Studio, and FiftyOne Enterprise connect through a custom endpoint |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Segments.ai samples, and Label Studio when presigned mode is on. Maximum expiry is 7 days |
| CORS | Yes | Exact-origin GET/HEAD for browser-loaded media ([cors-labeling.json](examples/cors-labeling.json)) |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Large point-cloud and export uploads (client-managed) |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Tool readers on `anonymized/`; separate writers for `labels/` |
| Event Notifications | Yes | `labels/` ObjectCreated starts validation |
| Object versions | Yes | Protect label exports from overwrite |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Expire anonymized and pre-label working copies after a campaign |
| SSE-B2 | Yes | Default encryption |
| SSE-C | No | Browser tools and presigned URLs cannot supply customer-key headers |
| Object Lock | Optional | Label releases that feed safety-relevant models |
| Cloud Replication | No | Not part of this flow |
| Included egress, CDN, compute partners | Partly | Annotator reads are B2 egress; check [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard | Annotator latency depends on the tool and browser path, not on Overdrive |

## Configure the integrations

Derive `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` from the labeling bucket's region.

### CVAT

- Attach cloud storage with the **AWS S3** provider. Set the **Endpoint URL** to the B2 endpoint, then enter the bucket and a key pair, as in the [CVAT docs](https://docs.cvat.ai/docs/workspace/attach-cloud-storage/), whose Backblaze B2 section marks the Endpoint URL as required for B2, and the [Backblaze CVAT guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-connect-backblaze-b2-cloud-storage-to-cvat).
- Key: `listBuckets,listFiles,readFiles` (`listBuckets` permits the CVAT `HeadBucket` check), scoped to `<org>-av-label` and `anonymized/`. Import pre-labels through CVAT's annotation import, and write exports with a separate `labels/` writer.
- CVAT rejects endpoints that resolve to private IP ranges, so self-hosted CVAT needs to reach the public B2 endpoint.

### Label Studio

- Add **Amazon S3** source storage. Set the optional **S3 Endpoint** to B2, set the bucket prefix to `anonymized/<campaign>/`, and use a read-only key. Add a separate target storage on `labels/<campaign>/` with a `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles` key ([Label Studio S3 storage](https://labelstud.io/guide/storage_s3)).
- With presigned URLs on, annotator browsers fetch from B2 directly and need CORS. With them off, Label Studio proxies the media and no CORS rule is needed.

### Segments.ai

- Use **customer-secured URLs**. Your service signs GET URLs with a read-only `anonymized/` key and registers them as sample attributes. Segments stores only the URL references ([import data](https://docs.segments.ai/how-to-integrate/import-data)).
- SigV4 presigned URLs expire after at most 7 days. Either size campaigns to fit, or refresh the URLs for open samples before they expire.
- Segments.ai's cross-account cloud integration is AWS-specific; use customer-secured URLs for B2. Add the Segments.ai web app origin to the bucket CORS rule.

### Encord

- Use a **Direct Access** integration. Your service signs GET URLs with a read-only `anonymized/` key, writes them as `objectUrl` values in the registration JSON, and registers the files through the UI or SDK ([Direct Access integration](https://docs.encord.com/platform-documentation/General/annotate-data-integrations/annotate-direct-access-integration)). Add a CORS rule for the Encord app origin.
- With strict client-only access, include per-file metadata in the JSON; Encord then does not store the files on its servers.
- Re-sign URLs before the SigV4 7-day maximum for campaigns that run longer.
- Alternative: Encord's S3-compatible [MinIO integration](https://docs.encord.com/platform-documentation/General/annotate-data-integrations/annotate-minIO-integration) takes an access key pair, and its SDK addresses S3-compatible storage as `https://<endpoint>/<bucket>/<path>`. Use it with a read-only `anonymized/` key when your policy lets Encord hold a key and sign URLs itself.

### FiftyOne Enterprise

- Configure a MinIO credentials profile: `MINIO_ENDPOINT_URL` set to the B2 endpoint, or an ini file with `endpoint_url`, plus the key pair and region ([installation](https://docs.voxel51.com/enterprise/installation.html)). Media paths then use that endpoint as their prefix.
- Use a read-only key for QA. Write saved views or tags to FiftyOne's own database, not to B2.
- Open-source FiftyOne loads media from local paths. Sync the campaign slice to local disk with rclone before loading it there.

## Security

- **No raw access for labeling tools.** Labeling tool keys are scoped to `anonymized/` (plus `prelabels/` with a second key if a tool reads pre-labels directly). They never cover `raw/` or `extracted/`. See [examples/README.md](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys).
- Export writers can write only `labels/<campaign>/`. The validator gets read-only access to `labels/`.
- CORS lists exact HTTPS origins and allows only `s3_get` and `s3_head`. Never use `*` on a bucket that holds people's images.
- Presigned URLs given to an external vendor are bearer credentials. Keep their expiry to the labeling window, and rotate the signing key to revoke all outstanding URLs if necessary.
- Restrict who can add storage connections in each tool, because the endpoint and key determine what the tool's server can read.

## Compliance

- Anonymize before external access. Record the anonymization model, version, and thresholds in the label release manifest.
- Keep un-blurred frames inside `raw/` and `extracted/`, with access limited to the extraction and anonymization roles.
- Align vendor data-processing agreements with where frames are served from (the B2 bucket region) and with what the vendor retains (URL references and labels).

## References

- [B2 CORS rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-cross-origin-resource-sharing-rules)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)
- [B2 Event Notifications reference](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-event-notifications-reference-guide)
- [B2 server-side encryption](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-server-side-encryption)
- [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)

<!-- source: architectures/perception-training-data-checkpoints/architecture.md -->

# Version perception datasets, stream them to training, and track checkpoints

## Workload

Perception teams assemble labeled scenarios into datasets for 3D detection, segmentation, tracking, and occupancy. A dataset ranges from tens of terabytes to petabytes and changes with every labeling campaign. Teams need to:

- reproduce any model from the exact drives, labels, anonymization version, and splits it was trained on;
- stream shards to multi-node GPU training without staging full copies on each node;
- persist checkpoints durably during long runs and keep released models and datasets for audit.

B2 holds the dataset versions, checkpoints, and run artifacts. lakeFS or DVC pins the versions, Ray Train streams and checkpoints, and MLflow tracks the runs.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  LBL[(labels/campaign/version/)] --> ASM[Dataset assembler]
  SCN[(scenarios/set/version/)] --> ASM
  ASM -->|shards first, manifest.json last| DS[(B2 datasets bucket<br/>datasets/name/version/)]
  DS <-->|branch, commit| LFS[lakeFS<br/>metadata DB off B2]
  DS -.->|or pin manifests| DVC[DVC remote<br/>git pointers]
  DS -->|per-worker streaming GETs| RAY[Ray Train / PyTorch<br/>NVMe cache]
  RAY -->|checkpoints, multipart| CK[(B2 work bucket<br/>checkpoints/run/)]
  RAY -->|metrics, eval reports, models| MLF[MLflow tracking server<br/>DB off B2]
  MLF -->|b2:// artifacts| ART[(B2 work bucket<br/>mlflow/)]
  DS -->|server-side copy on release| REL[(B2 release bucket<br/>Object Lock)]
  ART -->|released model| REL
  DS -->|presigned GET, read-only key| PARTNER[Partner or supplier]
```

A version is complete only when its `manifest.json` exists. The manifest lists every shard with its size and SHA-256, the source scenario-set and label versions, the anonymization version, and the split definitions. Consumers ignore a version directory that has no manifest.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Datasets | `<org>-av-datasets/datasets/<name>/<version>/` | Immutable versions; keep | No (the release copy is locked) | WebDataset or Parquet shards plus the manifest |
| lakeFS storage namespace | `<org>-av-datasets/lakefs/<repo>/` | lakeFS garbage collection deletes; a hidden-only B2 rule reclaims what it deleted ([lifecycle-datasets.json](examples/lifecycle-datasets.json)) | No | lakeFS-managed objects |
| Checkpoints | `<org>-av-train/checkpoints/<run>/` | Hide after N days, then delete ([lifecycle-train-sim.json](examples/lifecycle-train-sim.json)). Size N above the longest expected run plus its resume window | No | Intermediate checkpoints |
| MLflow artifacts | `<org>-av-train/mlflow/` | Keep; prune by run policy | No | Metrics files, evaluation reports, registered models |
| Release | `<org>-av-release/datasets/…`, `<org>-av-release/models/…` | Never expire while locked | Governance default ([object-lock-evidence.json](examples/object-lock-evidence.json)) | Released dataset and model versions for lineage audits |

Copy a checkpoint to the release bucket before the lifecycle rule on `checkpoints/` hides it. Lifecycle applies to the whole prefix and cannot tell which checkpoints were promoted, or which run is still active: a hidden file is not listed, so Ray cannot resume from it. Size `daysFromUploadingToHiding` above the longest expected run plus pause and resume time, or write active runs under a separate prefix (for example `active/<run>/`) with no hide rule and move finished runs under `checkpoints/`.

Never set `daysFromUploadingToHiding` on `lakefs/`. lakeFS garbage collection deletes objects with `DeleteObject` and no version ID, which on B2 only hides them, so the hidden-only rule is what reclaims the storage ([why](examples/README.md#why-warehouse-and-lakefs-get-hidden-only-rules)).

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| lakeFS metadata | PostgreSQL or DynamoDB-compatible KV, per lakeFS docs | Transactional commit graph |
| MLflow tracking data | MLflow backend database | Runs, params, and metrics are small and mutable |
| Shard cache and dataloader scratch | Local NVMe on GPU nodes | Repeated epochs re-read hot shards |
| Orchestration | Ray head, Kubernetes | Control plane |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | Ray, MLflow (S3 mode), lakeFS, and DVC all use a custom endpoint |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | Dataset delivery to partners from a read-only key scoped to one version |
| CORS | No | No browser access |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Multi-GB checkpoints and shards (client-managed) |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Training reader on `datasets/`; checkpoint writer; MLflow writer; release publisher |
| Event Notifications | Optional | Start dataset validation when `manifest.json` lands |
| Object versions | Yes | Overwrite protection for manifests |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Expire intermediate checkpoints; reclaim objects lakeFS GC deleted |
| SSE-B2 | Yes | Default encryption |
| Object Lock | Yes | Release bucket |
| Server-side copy | Yes | Promote dataset versions and models into the release bucket without re-uploading |
| Cloud Replication | No | Add only for a DR requirement; it is bucket-to-bucket, not delivery |
| Included egress, CDN, compute partners | Yes | Training on GPU clouds reads B2 directly; check [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) for current egress terms |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard plus NVMe cache by default | Measure GPU utilization first. Consider [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) when sustained multi-node read throughput is the proven bottleneck |

## Configure the integrations

Derive `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` from each bucket's region.

### Ray (Train)

- Set `RunConfig(storage_path="s3://<org>-av-train/checkpoints?endpoint_override=https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com")`, or set `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` with a plain `s3://` path. The [Ray persistent-storage guide](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html) gives this form with a Backblaze B2 example.
- Keys: the checkpoint writer key covers `checkpoints/` with `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,deleteFiles`. Ray reads checkpoints back to resume, and `num_to_keep` deletes old ones. The dataset reader key is a separate read-only key on `datasets/`.
- Streaming: split shards per worker and per node, as in the [WebDataset Streaming PyTorch Training](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/webdataset-streaming-pytorch-training) sample.

### MLflow

- Native `b2://` artifact repository (`B2ArtifactRepository` is registered in MLflow's artifact-repository registry), or an `s3://` artifact root with `MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL` set to the B2 endpoint ([Backblaze MLflow guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-connect-backblaze-b2-to-mlflow), [artifact stores](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/)).
- Key: scoped to `mlflow/`. Prefer proxied artifact access (`--artifacts-destination`), so that only the tracking server holds the key and clients do not.

### lakeFS

- Set `blockstore.type: s3`, `blockstore.s3.endpoint` to the B2 endpoint, `blockstore.s3.force_path_style: true`, and the region and credentials ([lakeFS configuration](https://docs.lakefs.io/reference/configuration/), [Backblaze lakeFS guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lakefs-integration-with-backblaze-b2)).
- Key: scoped to the lakeFS storage namespace prefix. lakeFS garbage collection needs delete permission on that prefix.
- The [lakeFS on B2 Quickstart](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/lakefs-on-b2-quickstart) sample shows branch, commit, and merge.

### DVC

- Run `dvc remote add` with an `s3://` URL, then `dvc remote modify <name> endpointurl https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` ([DVC S3 remote](https://doc.dvc.org/user-guide/data-management/remote-storage/amazon-s3)). Store credentials with `--local` so they stay out of git.
- DVC suits manifest-sized pointers and moderate datasets. lakeFS fits petabyte datasets that need branch semantics.

## Security

- Training clusters hold a read-only `datasets/` key and a `checkpoints/` writer key. They never hold release-bucket or Object Lock credentials. See [examples/README.md](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys).
- The release publisher key runs only in the release pipeline. Promotion is a server-side copy, so the key covers both the source (`<org>-av-datasets` or `<org>-av-train`) and `<org>-av-release` buckets with `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,writeFileRetentions` (plus `writeFileLegalHolds` where used). See [examples/README.md](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys).
- Partner delivery uses presigned GETs signed by a short-duration, read-only key scoped to `datasets/<name>/<version>/`. URL lists are secrets. Do not use Cloud Replication for delivery.
- Never put keys in `RunConfig` strings that get logged. Pass them through the environment or a secret store.

## References

- [Backblaze S3-compatible API](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-s3-compatible-api)
- [B2 application keys](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-application-keys)
- [B2 Object Lock](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-object-lock)
- [B2 lifecycle rules](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-lifecycle-rules)
- [S3 CopyObject on B2](https://www.backblaze.com/apidocs/s3-copy-object)
- [B2 pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing)

<!-- source: architectures/simulation-resim-evaluation/architecture.md -->

# Re-simulate real drives and synthetic scenarios against each stack build and keep comparable KPIs

## Workload

Every candidate build of the driving stack runs against a regression suite before release. The suite has two parts:

- **Log re-simulation (re-sim):** real drive splits are replayed into the new perception and planning build in open-loop or log-replay mode.
- **Synthetic simulation:** OpenSCENARIO or CARLA/ScenarioRunner scenarios render sensor data and vehicle state for closed-loop tests.

A run covers thousands of scenarios and produces terabytes of episodes. Each build's KPI tables (collisions, off-road events, lane keeping, comfort) must stay comparable across releases, and results for release candidates become safety-case evidence.

B2 holds scenario definitions, the frozen suite manifest, simulator outputs, and KPI tables. Workers get only the access they need: presigned URLs for raw splits and a write-only key for their output prefix.

## Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CI[CI system<br/>build N] -->|trigger| ORCH[Orchestrator<br/>e.g. Ray Core fan-out]
  SUITE[(B2 sim bucket<br/>suites/name/version/manifest.json)] --> ORCH
  SCN[(scenarios/set/version/)] --> SUITE
  ORCH -->|presigned GET URLs<br/>expiry > job, ≤ 7 days| RESIM[Re-sim workers<br/>pull or range-read to NVMe<br/>ros2 bag play]
  RAW[(B2 raw<br/>raw/…/*.mcap)] --> RESIM
  ORCH --> SIM[Simulator workers<br/>GPU render]
  CFG[(B2 sim bucket<br/>scenario-configs/)] --> SIM
  SIM -->|write-only key| EP[(B2 sim bucket<br/>sim/episodes/build/scenario/id/)]
  RESIM -->|KPI Parquet| RES[(B2 sim bucket<br/>sim/results/build/)]
  SIM -->|KPI Parquet| RES
  RES -->|log per build| MLF[MLflow<br/>b2:// artifacts]
  RES -->|release candidate:<br/>server-side copy| EVID[(B2 evidence bucket<br/>Object Lock)]
  EP -->|curated episodes| DS[Training datasets]
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant CI as CI
  participant O as Orchestrator
  participant B as B2
  participant W as Re-sim worker
  CI->>O: Run suite v7 on build N
  O->>B: GET suites/v7/manifest.json
  O->>O: Sign GET URLs for referenced splits (read-only raw key, held by O only)
  O->>W: Task(scenario, URLs, output prefix)
  W->>B: GET split (presigned) to NVMe
  W->>W: ros2 bag play to stack build N
  W->>B: PUT sim/results/N/<scenario>.parquet (write-only key)
  O->>B: CopyObject results to evidence bucket (release candidates only)
```

rosbag2 does not read over HTTP, so workers download or range-read each split to local NVMe before replay. Presigned URLs expire after at most 7 days. Long-queued jobs must request fresh URLs rather than relying on URLs signed at submission time.

## B2 zones

| Zone | Bucket and prefix | Versioning and lifecycle | Object Lock | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw (input) | `<org>-av-raw/raw/` | See [drive-log offload](architectures/drive-log-offload-ingest/architecture.md) | Optional | Real drive splits |
| Scenario configs | `<org>-av-sim/scenario-configs/<set>/<version>/` | Immutable versions | No | OpenSCENARIO or CARLA JSON |
| Suites | `<org>-av-sim/suites/<name>/<version>/manifest.json` | Immutable | No | Frozen regression suite (scenario and split references) |
| Episodes | `<org>-av-sim/sim/episodes/<build>/<scenario>/<id>/` | Hide after N days, then delete ([lifecycle-train-sim.json](examples/lifecycle-train-sim.json)) | No | Bulk synthetic RGB, depth, segmentation, LiDAR, and state |
| Results | `<org>-av-sim/sim/results/<build>/` | Keep | No | Per-run KPI Parquet |
| Evidence | `<org>-av-evidence/sim-results/<build>/` | Never expire while locked | Governance default | Release-candidate results for the safety case |

Episodes and results sit under different top-level paths (`sim/episodes/` and `sim/results/`) because B2 lifecycle rules match name prefixes. One rule can then expire bulk frames while KPI tables stay.

## Boundaries

| Stays off B2 | Where it lives | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Simulator GPU servers and render state | GPU nodes | Compute |
| Scenario scheduler and queue | Ray head or a queue service | Control plane |
| CI system | CI | Triggers runs, gates releases |
| MLflow tracking database | MLflow backend database | Run metadata |
| Results dashboard database | Analytics database | Interactive queries; B2 holds the Parquet source |

## B2 capability map

| Capability | Used | How |
|---|---|---|
| S3-compatible API | Yes | MLflow, the orchestrator (URL signing), and workers through an S3 SDK |
| Presigned URLs | Yes | GET URLs for raw splits so workers hold no raw key |
| CORS | No | No browser access |
| Range GETs | Yes | Partial split reads using the MCAP chunk index |
| Multipart upload | Yes | Large episode files (client-managed) |
| Scoped application keys | Yes | Orchestrator raw reader; worker writer on `sim/`; release copier |
| Event Notifications | Optional | Start the KPI roll-up when the last result lands |
| Object versions | Yes | Overwrite protection for suites and results |
| Lifecycle rules | Yes | Expire `sim/episodes/` |
| SSE-B2 | Yes | Default encryption |
| Object Lock | Yes | Evidence bucket |
| Cloud Replication | No | Not part of this flow |
| Included egress, CDN, compute partners | Yes | GPU simulation farms read B2 directly; check [pricing](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/pricing) |
| Standard B2 vs Overdrive vs local cache | Standard plus NVMe | Splits are read once per scenario. Consider [Overdrive](https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/b2-overdrive) only if measured suite wall-clock time is bound by storage reads |

## Configure the integrations

Derive `https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` from each bucket's region.

### Orchestrator (Ray Core or a queue)

- Ray Core (or any scheduler) only fans out tasks; it has no B2 connection of its own and no `storage_path`. Ray Train's persistent storage, described in the [training architecture](architectures/perception-training-data-checkpoints/architecture.md#ray-train), does not apply here.
- The orchestrator holds the read-only raw key, used only to sign URLs. Workers get presigned URLs and a write-only `sim/` key, and move bytes with an S3 SDK (B2 pattern).

### MLflow

- Log one run per (build, suite version), with KPI tables and reports as artifacts in a `b2://` store or an `s3://` store with `MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL` ([Backblaze MLflow guide](https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-connect-backblaze-b2-to-mlflow)).
- Tag each run with the build ID, suite version, and simulator version so results stay comparable.

### Simulator and rosbag2 workers

Workers transfer CARLA, ScenarioRunner, and rosbag2 inputs and outputs with an S3 SDK or presigned URLs. The [CARLA Sensor Data Lake](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/carla-sensor-data-lake) and [Rosbag2 Cloud Offload](https://github.com/backblaze-b2-samples/rosbag2-cloud-offload) samples show this.

## Security

- Workers never hold a raw-bucket key. A leaked worker credential exposes only its presigned URLs and write access to `sim/`.
- Only the release pipeline's publisher key can write to the evidence bucket. The evidence copy is a server-side copy, so that key covers both `<org>-av-sim` and `<org>-av-evidence` with `listFiles,readFiles,writeFiles,writeFileRetentions` (plus `writeFileLegalHolds` where used). See [examples/README.md](examples/README.md#scoped-application-keys).
- Don't log presigned URLs. Redact query strings in worker logs.
- Store a checksum with every result file, and reference results in the evidence bucket by version ID.
